source.title: Large batch size training of neural networks with adversarial training and second-order information
source.authors: Zhe-Wei Yao; A. Gholami; Daiyaan Arfeen; Richard Liaw; Joseph E. Gonzalez; K. Keutzer; Michael W. Mahoney

record.tranche_reason: The paper compares test accuracy across fixed and adaptive batch-size training, using its own experiments and methods to examine the large-batch generalization gap.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test-accuracy results for batch-size and training-method comparisons. It also discusses prior work, which is not recorded as this paper's own result. Hessian-curvature plots and measurements are recorded under fits_no_version because they do not measure the magnitude-aware sharpness specified in V7.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares held-out accuracy across fixed batch sizes at fixed epoch budgets and tests whether adaptive batches, learning-rate scaling, warmup and adversarial training preserve accuracy. These results test V5; the study is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors conclude that Hessian-guided adaptive batches, combined with adversarial training and an elastic Ray framework, permit earlier batch increases and fewer SGD updates while generally maintaining comparable accuracy. Warmup tuning further reduces updates. Their accuracy-preservation claim is approximate: CIFAR-100 ABS and ImageNet ResNet18 retain numerical deficits, and Hessian computation adds overhead.
record.recipe_differences: Tests adaptive batch-size schedules and adversarial training against fixed-batch SGD and other batch-size schedules; it does not reproduce the cited large-batch studies' experimental protocols exactly.
record.method_sensitivity: Accuracy changes with fixed batch size and training method; the paper reports different outcomes for ABS versus ABSA, dataset/model, and tuned versus untuned warm-up schedules.

fits_no_version.finding: Loss-surface interpolation and dominant-Hessian-direction perturbations show larger curvature for large-batch trajectories than for small-batch SGD or ABSA.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unscaled Hessian curvature and training trajectories accompany differences in held-out accuracy across batch-size recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: The convex convergence theorem and mushroom logistic-regression experiment concern optimization loss and iteration efficiency.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive batches with scaled learning rates can accelerate optimization under the specified assumptions.

record.problems: The paper states that ImageNet experiments were limited by computational resources and did not run GG. It reports no error bars or significance estimates for the accuracy comparisons. TinyImageNet accuracy is validation accuracy, and the text notes that this set is sometimes called a test set. The text gives inconsistent update-reduction ratios for the Cifar-10 tuned result: 48.1× in Section IV-C and 44.8× in the abstract and conclusion.
record.rows_left_out: The tables report many intermediate fixed batch sizes and method-by-batch accuracy values. To stay within the row limit and keep the main contrasts, intermediate table entries and most per-batch ABS/ABSA entries were not extracted; see Tables I and III-VIII. Also omitted: timing and SGD-update-count outcomes, which do not measure test error.

untested.parts: Fitting random labels and contrasting held-out performance with natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and learned local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under different tuning budgets; adaptive batch size is not an adaptive optimizer comparison.
Language models; longer training as an isolated intervention; normalization changes; equal-epoch recovery for the tuned ImageNet experiment; a constant-large-batch ImageNet control.
Dropout interventions and their interaction with dataset size, augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, generalization-gap ranking among similarly fitted networks, and comparisons against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing random examples.

missing.what: Add SVHN's omitted workload-level contrast: S1 trained for 20 epochs reaches 94.90% at fixed batch 128, 95.17% at 2048, and 84.75% at 131072; at maximum batch 131072, GG, ABS and ABSA reach 95.58%, 95.61% and 95.92%. The declared omissions cover intermediate entries, not this entire workload's principal contrast.

record.verdict_notes: Recovery under an adapted recipe supports a clause already present in V5; it does not by itself challenge that version. States for adaptive rows refer to the recovery clause, while states for fixed-batch contrasts refer to the penalty. Baseline-only rows are retained as references. Intermediate table entries and most method-by-batch results are already declared omitted. No reported error bars establish whether small accuracy differences are significant.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Language models; batch-size threshold characterization across workloads; comparisons under a fixed epoch budget for every reported method.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness and comparisons against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.
